biggest_gap.title: Filtering the audit log by who made the change does not work: typing a person's name gives a 400 and the list stays unfiltered
biggest_gap.detail: The spec asks for a global audit log 'with filters by user, record type, record, field and date'. Record type, field, record and date filters all work by keyboard in English and Arabic, and fast (110 to 480 ms on 740,000 rows). The 'Changed by' column filter is a plain text box, because the column is a reference with no options (AuditLogPage passes only a label lookup). Whatever you type is sent as actorId eq '<text>'. A name such as 'Noor Editor' is answered 400, the screen shows 'Some fields need attention. Try again', and the grid keeps every row (740,644). The only working way to filter by person is to find one of that person's changes first and open it: its side panel has 'Every change by <name>'. Answering 'what did this employee change last week' is a daily job for a UAE trading company's accountant or auditor, so this matters. Fix: a person picker for the filter (users by name, as the users list's own search finds them) or a name search on the server. This is separate from what blocks the round: two failing G1 tests from p11's attachments probe; see hard_gates and other_findings.
biggest_gap.evidence: browser/walk5.mjs (en '[["Changed by","Noor Editor","type"]]'), output in this verdict: 400 http://localhost:20750/api/audit/log?filter=actorId+eq+%27Noor+Editor%27&sort=-occurredAt&take=100. Screenshot en-06-filter-Changedby.jpg shows the chip 'Changed by is Noor Editor', the red 'Some fields need attention' banner and the unfiltered rows. Definition: /api/lists/audit.log/definition gives actorId type 'reference' with no choices (attack/def.mjs).

other_findings: [route: p11-attachments] What blocks this round: G1AttachmentsAttackTests and G1HttpIsolationTests both failed in the clean-clone verify with 'contacts.contacts: the victim has no file to defend (its seeded files are missing)' from AttachmentsIsolationProbe.cs:136. G1AttachmentsAttackTests passes run alone at the same commit (1 m 48 s). Suspected cause: the probe looks for tenant B's files only on the first page of B's active contacts, while the files sit on the first 3 contacts by NameEn (archived ones included), and B's concurrent own writes (create, archive, restore of contacts) change that page. The probe should look up the seeded files' own records rather than the list's first page. This is the first time it has been seen; serial-19's runs at b9f63bf1 did not show it. Never skip or loosen it.

Tamper evidence (audit, CLAUDE.md rule 4): erp_app still holds INSERT on audit.entries, and the capture function is not the only writer. As erp_app the critic inserted a made-up audit row in its own tenant with a random actor_id and occurred_at set 400 days back; it succeeded (rolled back, attack/db-role.out). Round 2 found the same. Round 3's fix (SECURITY DEFINER trigger, INSERT revoked) was backed out in e6d80e84.

[route: p11-attachments] Attachment audit rows are readable with audit.log.read alone: attachments.files is registered with AuditPermissions.LogRead, not the read permission of the parent record. A role holding only identity.roles.read and audit.log.read sees the file names, checksums and contact ids of files attached to contacts it cannot read (attack/att.mjs, att.out: 'Trade licence TL-2026-70005.pdf' on a contact). p07 added ParentKindField/ParentIdField in round 4 but VisibleAsync does not use them to require the parent's read permission.

Export columns do not match the screen: in the CSV, XLSX and PDF export of audit.log, 'Fields' is a count ('6', '1'), while the screen shows the field names (round 2 found the same). The list's own 'Fields' column also shows '1' for a custom-field change instead of its name (en-04-audit-log.jpg, the Credit review date row).

'Old and new values' still shows raw ISO timestamps for sign-in sessions ('Expires: 2026-11-14T23:37:59.115984+00:00'), in Arabic with a stray word ('ينتهي في: القيمة 2026-11-14T23:48:09…'); round 2 found the same (en-04, ar-04). Sign-in sessions are still most of the newest rows in the log.

One keyboard save of a contact that changes a standard field and a custom field writes 3 audit rows in one transaction (job_title; custom_fields.cfCreditReview; and a customfields.field_values row named by its key 'cfCreditReview', even in Arabic). The line under the record's heading then shows only the custom field change and hides the job title change from the same save (en-03-after-keyboard-save.jpg; attack/hist.mjs).
The Fields filter lists duplicate labels (Name x2, Name in Arabic x2, Currency x2, Digits x2), so the user cannot tell which field they are choosing (browser/walk5 output).

Export speed is fixed since round 2. On the demo with 740,655 rows: CSV 6.5 s, XLSX 7.0 s, PDF English 26 s, PDF Arabic 59 s (154 MB); round 2 measured PDF at 360 s. Exports stop at 200,000 rows with a notice row (attack/export-timing.out). The list opens in 324 ms with 740,641 rows counted, and the contact history panel (Alt+Y, Escape gives focus back) works in English and Arabic (RTL).

[route: p01-odoo-rig] The comparison harness's round-14 set-up guard (lib/sandbox/bridge.mjs setUpCarries) refuses any set-up save of a contact in ours, because our PUT /api/contacts/contacts/{id} needs the whole record (the name included). So who-changed-field cannot do its own set-up on ours. The critic's driver checks a change made just before the run instead (driver/ours-who-changed-field.mjs). p01 is frozen; a future builder of the ours driver needs a fixture rule for this, or a partial-update endpoint from p16.
